issues.legal_issue: Retirement from service falls within the service-ending events that permit summary recovery of railway property detained by a former railway servant.
material_facts: The employee received the premises as official accommodation because of his railway employment.
He retained possession after retiring from service.
The railway administration applied for summary recovery of the premises.
issues.conclusion: Retirement is included within the meaning of discharge in Section 138, so the summary procedure may be invoked when a former employee retains railway property and refuses or neglects to return it after written notice.
issues.legal_principle: Section 138 of the Indian Railways Act, 1890 provides a speedy summary procedure for recovery of railway property detained by a railway servant or legal representative. The provision is to be construed broadly to advance its purpose. In Union of India v. B.N. Prasad, the Court held that discharge under Section 138 has wide amplitude; S.L. Kapoor v. Emperor, Divisional Superintendent, Eastern Railway v. Suresh Chandra Chakravarty, and Arjun Babloo Tukaral v. G.V. Javalkar support treating termination of service, including retirement, as discharge.

rule.if: summary_recovery_proceeding and property_provided_due_to_service and service_relationship_ended and former_employee_retained_property and refusal_after_written_notice

predicates.summary_recovery_proceeding: The railway administration brought a proceeding seeking summary recovery of property.
predicates.property_provided_due_to_service: The railway administration provided the property to the employee because of the employee's service.
predicates.service_relationship_ended: The employment relationship ended, including by retirement, resignation, dismissal, removal, or another form of discharge.
predicates.former_employee_retained_property: The former employee continued to possess the property after the employment relationship ended.
predicates.refusal_after_written_notice: After receiving written notice to return the property, the former employee or a representative refused or neglected to return it.

issues.definition: When a summary recovery proceeding concerns property provided because of service and retained after the service relationship ends despite written notice, summary recovery is available.

issues.legal_issue: A licensee who received possession of property from the railway administration as official accommodation cannot deny the administration's title while possession has not been surrendered, and the administration need not prove the precise nature of its interest against that licensee.
material_facts: The employee was given possession of the premises as official accommodation while serving the railway administration.
The employee did not surrender possession after retirement.
The employee disputed the railway administration's entitlement on the ground that it had not proved its lease of the premises.
issues.conclusion: The employee was estopped from denying the railway administration's title; the administration was not required in these proceedings to prove whether it owned, leased, mortgaged, or held the premises under another interest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 prevents a person who entered immovable property under a licence from denying the title of the person in possession when the licence was granted. The estoppel continues until the licensee openly restores possession by surrender or is evicted. The Court relied on S. Thangappan v. P. Padmavathy and Vashu Deo v. Balkishan, which discuss the scope and duration of landlord-tenant estoppel; Vashu Deo also refers to Currimbhoy & Co. Ltd. v. L.A. Creet and Bilas Kunwar v. Desraj Ranjit Singh.

predicates.summary_recovery_proceeding: The property holder brought a proceeding seeking summary recovery of the property.
predicates.property_possession_granted_under_servic: The person in possession entered the property under a licence granted by the person then in possession, including as service accommodation.
predicates.licensee_has_not_surrendered_possession: The licensee has not openly restored possession to the person who granted the licence.

issues.definition: When a licensee entered property under a licence and has not surrendered possession, the licensee cannot deny the title of the person who granted the licence in a summary recovery proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A proceeding for summary recovery of railway property does not empower the court to award mesne profits.
material_facts: The railway administration sought mesne profits for the period of the former employee's continued possession after retirement.
The claim had not been raised before the trial court.
The proceeding was brought under the summary recovery procedure.
issues.conclusion: The mesne-profits claim could not be decided in the summary recovery proceeding, and the railway administration remained free to pursue another remedy available under law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 138 of the Indian Railways Act, 1890 authorizes summary recovery of property but does not empower the court to award mesne profits in that proceeding. The Court also noted that the claim had not been raised before the trial court.

predicates.summary_recovery_proceeding: The case is a proceeding seeking summary recovery of property.
predicates.mesne_profit_claim: A party seeks mesne profits for another party's period of possession.
predicates.claim_not_raised_at_trial: The mesne-profits claim was not raised before the trial court.

issues.definition: When a mesne-profits claim is made in a summary recovery proceeding but was not raised at trial, the claim is left for another legal remedy rather than decided in that proceeding.
